title: Similar Triangles

findings.finding: In the supplied booklet order, p7-q6 introduces unknown-side calculation together with an hourglass configuration and angle equalities inferred from parallel lines.
findings.breakdown: Students must identify triangles within a combined figure, establish correspondence using angle relationships, and calculate an unknown corresponding length at their first application of proportional side calculation.
findings.checked: The preceding teaching and practice establish similarity tests, correspondence and numerical side ratios, but do not bridge this combined demand. The later p7-q5 supplies the missing intermediate task using separate right triangles.
findings.assumptions: Prior angle relationships and proportional reasoning are available from the course library. This finding concerns the supplied block order and does not depend on calculator use.

repair.proposal: Move p7-q5 immediately before p7-q6, introducing unknown-side calculation in separate triangles before the hourglass configuration.

findings.doneWhen: Students complete p7-q5 before attempting p7-q6.

findings.finding: Extend the existing construction with numerical calculations connecting the altitude and the two segments of the hypotenuse.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up applies the similarity correspondence already established in p10-q14 to concrete lengths.
findings.checked: With BC=6, AC=8 and AB=10, CD=6×8/10=4.8. Similarity gives AD/AC=AC/AB, so AD=6.4; BD=10−6.4=3.6. All required methods are available by this point.
findings.assumptions: The additional numerical givens apply to all three new parts.

repair.proposal: After p10-q14-b, add: “For parts (c)–(e), let a=6, b=8 and c=10. (c) Find CD. (d) Find AD using triangle ABC similar to triangle ACD. (e) Find BD.” Expected answers: (c) 4.8; (d) 6.4; (e) 3.6.

findings.doneWhen: The three numerical follow-up parts appear after p10-q14-b with the shared numerical givens.

findings.finding: Extend the nested-triangle question by comparing increases in corresponding side lengths.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up connects the scale factor with the difference between corresponding lengths.
findings.assumptions: Students complete p7-q7-b first. The extension adds only subtraction and ratio comparison to the methods that question already requires.

repair.proposal: Append to p7-q7: c Find DE. Answer: 4 cm. d Find CD:DE. Answer: 2:1. e Find BD:(AE−BD). Answer: 2:1. f Explain why the ratios in d and e are equal. Expected answer: each larger corresponding length is 1.5 times the smaller length, so each increase is half the smaller length.

findings.doneWhen: The follow-up appears after p7-q7-b, with each question presented as a separate part.

importReview: Lean content review table: 17 of 17 blocks passed.

dropped.reason: The proposed contrast fails the mathematical check. In (iii), AB=4, AC=6 and angle ABC=50° determine a unique triangle up to similarity, so the proportional second triangle is necessarily similar. In (iv), AC=6, AB=4 and angle ACB=50° are impossible: the sine rule would require sin B=1.5 sin 50°>1. Moreover, insufficient-information parts would conflict with p5-q3's existing instruction to choose a test proving that the pairs are similar.
